lead: Albany has some of the oldest housing in the country, with more than 40% of homes built before 1940. Old rowhouses, combined sewers and long winters keep water damage busy.
risk: basement backups, ice dams and leaks in old rowhouses
risk_short: basement backups, ice dams, old rowhouses
why: About 43% of Albany homes were built before 1940, and nearly 79% before 1980. Center Square, Park South and the Mansion District are full of brick rowhouses with shared walls, flat roofs and stone basements. Water from a neighbor's roof or pipe can cross into the next house. Only about 38% of homes are owner-occupied, so many leaks involve landlords and tenants.

Like its neighbors, Albany has combined sewers that carry both rain and sewage. In big storms they can overflow, and old house laterals can back up into basements. Under a 2014 agreement, Albany and five nearby communities began a long-term plan to cut those overflows. Winters bring heavy snow, ice dams on older roofs and frozen pipes in unheated spaces.
image_alt: Brick bungalow with a snow-covered roof and yard
image_caption: Ice dams and shared-wall leaks are common in Albany's older rowhouses.
problems: Center Square, Park South, Mansion District
tips: Install a backwater valve if your basement drain has backed up.
Have a flat rowhouse roof checked every year.
Add attic insulation and venting to cut ice dams.
Renters: report leaks to your landlord in writing.
areas: Calls come from Center Square, Pine Hills, Park South, Arbor Hill, the Mansion District, Helderberg, Delaware Avenue and the South End, plus Troy, Colonie and Guilderland.

faq.q: Who pays for water damage in an Albany rental?
faq.a: The landlord usually pays to fix the building, and the tenant's renters insurance covers their belongings. If a tenant caused the leak, their liability coverage may help. Report leaks in writing and take photos right away.

sources: NYS DEC: Combined sewer overflows and the Albany Pool
